title: Remote Follow-Up After Atrial Fibrillation Ablation
summary: This study evaluates whether digital follow-up after atrial fibrillation ablation works well in everyday practice. It assesses whether patients regularly complete measurements or app-based entries over 12 weeks. The study also records patient satisfaction, ease of use, changes in quality of life, and whether unplanned doctor visits, emergency contacts, or hospital readmissions occur.
conditions: Atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter, unspecified

interventions.name:
Inpatient ablation / app-based digital follow-up / non-randomised control group
Patients undergoing atrial fibrillation ablation in the conventional inpatient setting receive structured digital follow-up via the app/remote-monitoring platform without an additional vital-sign monitoring device.

Outpatient ablation – app-based follow-up without device / randomised 1:1:1 (Arm2-Arm4)
Patients undergoing outpatient atrial fibrillation ablation receive app-based digital follow-up only.

Outpatient ablation – app plus upper-arm blood pressure monitor with ECG function / randomised 1:1:1 (Arm2-Arm4)
Patients undergoing outpatient atrial fibrillation ablation use the app together with an upper-arm blood pressure monitor capable of single-lead ECG recording.

Outpatient ablation – app plus wearable wristband with vital-sign and ECG monitoring / randomised 1:1:1 (Arm2-Arm4)
Patients undergoing outpatient atrial fibrillation ablation use the app together with a wearable wristband for vital-sign and ECG monitoring.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Recent atrial fibrillation ablation
Access to a smartphone and ability to perform daily measurements or app-based study procedures
Written informed consent and willingness to participate and comply with study instructions
Exclusion criteria:
Life expectancy < 3 months due to non-cardiac disease
Cognitive, physical, or language limitations preventing completion of study procedures or valid informed consent
Concurrent participation in another interventional study that could confound the study outcomes
Investigator assessment that participation cannot be conducted safely
